'''''Hesperantha coccinea''''', the '''river lily''', or '''crimson flag lily''',<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/142724/Hesperantha-coccinea/Details | title = ''Hesperantha coccinea'' | website = www.rhs.org | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 17 August 2020}}</ref>  [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] '''''Schizostylis coccinea''''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the iris [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Iridaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to Southern Africa and Zimbabwe.<ref name=POWO>{{cite web |url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:991373-1 |title= Hesperantha coccinea (Backh. & Harv.) Goldblatt & J.C.Manning |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=November 29, 2024}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url= https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/3L482 |title= Hesperantha coccinea (Backh. & Harv.) Goldblatt & J.C.Manning |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=November 29, 2024}}</ref> It is a semi[[evergreen]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] growing to {{convert|60|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall, with slender lanceolate [[leaf|leaves]] up to {{convert|40|cm|0|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|1|cm|abbr=on|1}} broad. The [[flower]]s are red, occasionally pink or white, 30–35 mm long, with six petals; they are produced four to ten alternately on a spike in late summer to autumn.

The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''coccinea'' means “bright red”.<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book |last=Harrison |first=Lorraine |title=RHS Latin for Gardeners |year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley |location=United Kingdom |isbn=184533731X }}</ref>

==Cultivation==
''Hesperantha coccinea'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]] in gardens for its flowers, It is often used in [[floristry]]. Hardy down to between {{convert|-5|and|-10|C|F|abbr=on}}, in colder regions it is grown under glass.<ref name=Huxl92>{{Citation |year=1992 |editor-last=Huxley |editor-first=A. |title=New RHS Dictionary of Gardening |publication-place=London |publisher=Macmillan |isbn=978-0-333-77018-4 }}</ref> It was formerly known in cultivation as "Kaffir lily", and is still occasionally referenced as such. However, "[[Kaffir (racial term)|Kaffir]]" is now regarded as an offensive [[ethnic slur]].

Numerous [[cultivars]] are available, of which the following have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]:-<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 48 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | website = www.rhs.org | accessdate = 3 March 2018}}</ref>
